children: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ($SOX) has moved above the 10,500 resistance area, extending its rebound from the early-November low.
The index stood at 10,631.16, above the level flagged by market analyst Mark Ungewitter in a post on X.

The dotted band around 10,500 marked a price area the index crossed during its advance in May and again during its decline from late October into November. The latest move has taken the benchmark back above that zone.

The broader chart puts the current level in a longer-term perspective. The SOX peaked near 14,500 in June and July, well above its October high near 13,000, leaving the index substantially below its summer peak.

The chart also captured the rally that preceded those highs. The index began the period around 8,000 in March, fell to roughly 7,000 in April, and then climbed through the spring and summer before its subsequent pullback.
The data also showed the SOX relative to the S&P 500 (
). The ratio, at 1.38, is testing the red line around 1.4 from below. That level held as support from roughly August through October before the ratio broke below it in November.
